subject: Re: Acme RFP — SLO measurement governance & evidence
messages:
From: Sophie Matthews <sophie.matthews@acme.com>

Subject: Acme RFP — initial SLO measurement clarifications

Jonas / team,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP. A few procurement and SRE items that need alignment before we move to the evidence request stage:

- Measurement basis: we need clarity whether Redwood will use synthetic probes, customer telemetry, or a blended approach for uptime/latency.
- Windowing: how are partial-region degradations accounted for (per-region weighting vs global window)?
- Sampling: what sampling cadence/percentile do you plan to use for p95/p99 latency calculations?
- Credits: how will fallback events (automated model downgrade, cross-region redirect) be excluded or included from credit calculations?

Could you provide a compact playbook (1–2 pages) that maps each policy to artifacts we can inspect (logs, probe configs, dashboards)? We’d like a timeline for delivering packaged evidence if Acme proceeds to vendor selection. I’ve attached our current RFP questions to make this concrete.

Appreciate a reply by EOD Monday so our SREs can triage.

Thanks,

Sophie Matthews
Director, Vendor Evaluation — Acme Corp
Sophie.Matthews@acme.com

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Matthews <sophie.matthews@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Acme RFP — initial SLO measurement clarifications

Sophie — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; we’ll package a 1–2 page playbook and an evidence manifest for you by next week. Attaching our current evidence matrix for reference.

1) Measurement basis: Redwood uses a blended approach by default. We run multi-region synthetic probes (active) plus an optional telemetry reconciliation pass against customer-observed telemetry (passive) for final adjudication. The probe fleet is configurable per-customer; you can choose probe-only (simpler), telemetry-only (if you want customer-only evidence), or blended (recommended for enterprise).

2) Windowing and region weighting: by default we calculate region-weighted availability (traffic-weighted) where each region’s probe results are weighted by historical production traffic share. We also support per-region SLAs if you prefer stricter boundaries.

3) Sampling & percentiles: latency percentiles are computed over tokenized request samples. We use stratified sampling by request size class and endpoint; default cadence is 1-minute aggregation with hourly sampling for p95/p99. We can provide raw sample dumps for audit.

4) Fallbacks/exclusions: automated model downgrades or planned cross-region failover are flagged as controlled fallbacks. Per the RFP, planned maintenance or explicit customer-triggered failovers are excluded from credits; automated fallbacks due to capacity constraints are included unless covered by a documented and agreed fallback policy.

Next steps: we’ll prepare the one-pager playbook (playbook includes where artifacts live, probe configs, sampling manifests, and example evidence), plus a packaged evidence bundle if you want a preview.

Attached: current-evidence-matrix.csv (columns: artifact, owner, retention, sample).

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Acme RFP — initial SLO measurement clarifications

Adding a few technical specifics from the prod/reliability side that will help Acme's SREs review faster: 

- Tokenized latency windows: for generation endpoints we measure latency both at request-level and token-append level (per-token delta) to catch tail behaviour caused by KV-cache misses. This matters for long-context workloads.
- Region weighting metric: traffic weighting is derived from the last 30 days of egress/ingress metrics unless the customer provides a preferred traffic matrix.
- Probe diversity: probes execute a mix of cold-start, warm-cache, and long-context traces to emulate customer mixes — we’ll share seed traces and probe schedules.
- Evidence packaging: our evidence bundle contains (1) probe results (time series + raw traces), (2) telemetry reconciliation reports (diffs between probes and customer logs), (3) replayable synthetic traces, and (4) a minimal audit-playlist to reproduce an incident.

We should propose two SKUs in the response: probe-only (shorter lead time) and blended (probe + telemetry reconciliation). Blended is the recommended path for any enterprise trying to avoid false positives/negatives.

—Lauren

Product Director, Reliability & Enterprise Integrations

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Matthews <sophie.matthews@acme.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Acme RFP — SLO measurement governance & evidence (playbook + example)

Sophie — Per your ask, attached is a consolidated 2-page playbook and an example incident pack. Short answers inline: 

- Redaction: we provide configurable column-level redaction and deterministic hashing for keys. Our evidence pipeline supports on-the-fly redaction before any bundle is exported; hashes are reversible to us for reconciliation under NDA but appear as hashed tokens to external reviewers.
- Retention: default retention for raw synthetic traces is 180 days; raw customer telemetry retention is configurable between 90–365 days per account (90 days meets your minimum). We include WALs for the reconciliation step for 30 days to support audits.
- Example downgrade: in the incident pack the downgrade appears as a timestamped event (automated: true) with related traces showing the model switch, latency delta, and traffic routed to fallback variant. Per our fallback policy, automated capacity-driven downgrades are included in availability calculations unless explicitly configured as permitted fallbacks in the contract. We included two scenarios (permitted vs non-permitted) in the incident pack with credit calculation examples.

Attachments: RI-SLO-Measurement-Playbook-v1.0.docx (playbook), example-incident-pack.zip (contains probe traces + reconciliation report).

Next: if Acme is happy with the playbook we will: (1) produce a signed evidence manifest; (2) propose the blended measurement SKU in the commercial appendix; (3) schedule a 60-minute technical walkthrough with your SREs (I can do Tue/Wed next week).

Link to the internal playbook & artifact locations: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ACME-RFP-7782-SLO-playbook

—Jonas
